Hardly comprehensible by the vulgar mind! But, even so, it is not the end of what I mean to give them. To-day I have racked their limbs; but I have yet to strike them to the heart, as they have stricken me!"

arxiv-1912-07878.title: Flash ionization signatures in the type Ibn supernova SN 2019uo
arxiv-1912-07878.creator: Anjasha Gangopadhyay, Kuntal Misra, Daichi Hiramatsu, Shan-Qin Wang, Griffin Hosseinzadeh, Xiaofeng Wang, Stefano Valenti, Jujia Zhang, D. Andrew Howell, Iair Arcavi, G.C. Anupama, Jamison Burke, Raya Dastidar, Koichi Itagaki, Brajesh Kumar, Brijesh Kumar, Long Li, Curtis McCully, Jun Mo, Shashi Bhu
arxiv-1912-07878.description: Abstract We present photometric and spectroscopic observations of the type Ibn supernova (SN) 2019uo, the second ever SN Ibn with flash ionization (He II, C III, N III) features in its early spectra. SN 2019uo displays a rapid post-peak luminosity decline of 0.

arxiv-2103-03042.title: New SU UMa-type star ZTF18abdlzhd in the Zwicky Transient Facility data Volume: 51
arxiv-2103-03042.creator: S.V. Antipin, A.M. Zubareva, A.A. Belinski, M.A. Burlak, N.P. Ikonnikova, K.L. Malanchev, M.V. Kornilov, E.O. Mishin
arxiv-2103-03042.description: Abstract We carried out a search for unknown dwarf novae in a public data release of the Zwicky Transient Facility survey and suspected that the object ZTF18abdlzhd is a SU UMa-type star. Performed multicolor CCD observations permit us to follow its fading from an outburst in August and an entire superoutburst in October 2020.

arxiv-2203-10939.creator: Abofazl Razi, Xiwen Chen, Hao WangSchool of ComputingClemson UniversityHuayu LiDepartment of Electrical and Computer EngineeringUniversity of ArizonaBrendan RussoDepartment of Civil EngineeringNorthern Arizona UniversityYan ChenThe Polytechnic SchoolArizona State UniversityHongbin YuSchool of Electr
arxiv-2203-10939.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Abofazl Razi, Xiwen Chen, Hao WangSchool of ComputingClemson UniversityHuayu LiDepartment of Electrical and Computer EngineeringUniversity of ArizonaBrendan RussoDepartment of Civil EngineeringNorthern Arizona UniversityYan ChenThe Polytechnic SchoolArizona State UniversityHongbin YuSchool of Electr. This paper explores Deep Learning (DL) methods that are used or have the potential to be used for traffic video analysis, emphasizing driving safety for both Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) and human-operated vehicles.

arxiv-2304-12711.title: Random model of flow decorrelation
arxiv-2304-12711.creator: Piotr Bożek, Hadi Mehrabpour
arxiv-2304-12711.description: Abstract The collective flow generated in relativistic heavy-ion collisions fluctuates from event to event. The fluctuations lead to a decorrelation of flow vectors measured in separate bins in phase space. These effects have been measured in experiments and observed in numerical simulations in hydrodynamic models. We present a simple random model of flow decorrelation in pseudorapidity.

arxiv-2308-00688.title: AnyLoc : Towards Universal Visual Place Recognition https://anyloc.github.io/
arxiv-2308-00688.creator: Nikhil Keetha, Avneesh Mishra, Jay Karhade, Krishna Murthy Jatavallabhula, Sebastian Scherer, Madhava Krishna, Sourav Garg, [5 pt] CMU, IIIT Hyderabad, MIT, University of Adelaide
arxiv-2308-00688.description: Abstract Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is vital for robot localization. To date, the most performant VPR approaches are environment- and task-specific : while they exhibit strong performance in structured environments (predominantly urban driving), their performance degrades severely in unstructured environments, rendering most approaches brittle to robust real-world deployment.

arxiv-2410-00943.title: RisingBALLER: A Player is a Token, a Match is a Sentence–A Path Towards a Foundational Model for Football Players Data Analytics
arxiv-2410-00943.creator: Akedjou Achraff ADJILEYE
arxiv-2410-00943.description: Abstract In this paper, I introduce RisingBALLER, the first publicly available approach that leverages a transformer model trained on football match data to learn match-specific player representations. Drawing inspiration from advances in language modeling, RisingBALLER treats each football match as a unique sequence in which players serve as tokens, with their embeddings shaped by the specific context of the match.

arxiv-2501-01600.title: Heavy quark suppression and anisotropic flow at intermediate momentum
arxiv-2501-01600.creator: Juhee Hong
arxiv-2501-01600.description: Abstract In an intermediate-momentum regime where mass effects are significant, heavy quark suppression and anisotropic flow are computed to investigate the transition between the collisional and radiative energy loss. Based on the collision kernel for diffusion, elastic scattering and semi-collinear gluon-bremsstrahlung can be consistently incorporated into a Boltzmann equation that involves the heavy quark diffusion coefficient.

arxiv-2502-12777.title: Evaluating link prediction: New perspectives and recommendations
arxiv-2502-12777.creator: Bhargavi Kalyani I, A Rama Prasad Mathi, Niladri Sett
arxiv-2502-12777.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bhargavi Kalyani I, A Rama Prasad Mathi, Niladri Sett. Link prediction (LP) is an important problem in network science and machine learning research. The state-of-the-art LP methods are usually evaluated in a uniform setup, ignoring several factors associated with the data and application specific needs.

arxiv-2505-06182.title: APPLE: Toward General Active Perception via Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2505-06182.creator: Tim Schneider, Cristiana de Farias, Roberto Calandra, Liming Chen, Jan Peters
arxiv-2505-06182.description: Abstract Active perception is a fundamental skill that enables us humans to deal with uncertainty in our inherently partially observable environment. For senses such as touch, where the information is sparse and local, active perception becomes crucial. In recent years, active perception has emerged as an important research domain in robotics.

arxiv-2506-11963.title: Conical Intersections and Electronic Momentum As Viewed From Phase Space Electronic Structure Theory
arxiv-2506-11963.creator: Titouan Duston, Nadine Bradbury, Zhen Tao, Joseph E. Subotnik
arxiv-2506-11963.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Titouan Duston, Nadine Bradbury, Zhen Tao, Joseph E. Subotnik. We investigate the structure of a prototypical two-state conical intersection (BeH 2 ) using a phase space electronic Hamiltonian H ^ P ​ S ​ ( 𝑹 , 𝑷 ) \hat{H}_{PS}({\bm{R}},{\bm{P}}) that goes beyond the Born-Oppenheimer framework.

arxiv-2602-20854.title: Adversarial Robustness on Insertion-Deletion Streams
arxiv-2602-20854.creator: Elena Gribelyuk, Honghao Lin, David P. Woodruff, Huacheng Yu, Samson Zhou
arxiv-2602-20854.description: Abstract We study adversarially robust algorithms for insertion-deletion (turnstile) streams, where future updates may depend on past algorithm outputs. While robust algorithms exist for insertion-only streams with only a polylogarithmic overhead in memory over non-robust algorithms, it was widely conjectured that turnstile streams of length polynomial in the universe size n n require space linear in n n .

pmc-10652897.title: Protein composition and nutritional aspects of pea protein fractions obtained by a modified isoelectric precipitation method using fermentation
pmc-10652897.creator: Mehrsa Emkani, Sylvie Moundanga, Bonastre Oliete, Rémi Saurel
pmc-10652897.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Pea albumins are promising for their nutritional, biological, and techno-functional properties. However, this fraction is usually discarded in the industry due to its low protein content compared to globulin fraction and the presence of some anti-nutritional compounds. In the present study, we used an alternative method of pea protein extraction based on alkaline solubilization/isoelectric precipitation in which the reduction of pH was achieved by lactic acid fermentation using specific starters instead of mineral acids.

pmc-11423735.title: Relationship between parents’ anxiety, stress, depression and their children’s health-related quality of life and psychological well-being during the COVID-19 outbreak in Iran
pmc-11423735.creator: Tao Liang, Mahlagha Dehghan, Yaser Soltanmoradi, Precious Chibuike Chukwuere, Hassan Pakdaman, Elham khaloobagheri, Mahmood Kahnooji, Seyedhamid Seyedbagheri, Mohammad Ali Zakeri
pmc-11423735.description: BackgroundIn late 2019, a new respiratory illness was detected in Wuhan, China and was later designated as COVID-19 by the WHO. Despite international efforts to impose restrictions and quarantine measures, the virus spreads rapidly across the globe. The pandemic has significantly impacted the mental health of both children and parents.

pmc-11449872.title: Empowering precision medicine: regenerative AI in breast cancer
pmc-11449872.creator: Sudip Bhattacharya, Sheikh Mohd Saleem, Alok Singh, Sukhpreet Singh, Shailesh Tripathi
pmc-11449872.description: Regenerative AI is transforming breast cancer diagnosis and treatment through enhanced imaging analysis, personalized medicine, drug discovery, and remote patient monitoring. AI algorithms can detect subtle patterns in mammograms and other imaging modalities with high accuracy, potentially leading to earlier diagnoses. In treatment planning, AI integrates patient-specific data to predict individual responses and optimize therapies.

pmc-11495950.title: The Pvc15 ATPase selectively associates effector proteins with the Photorhabdus virulence cassette
pmc-11495950.creator: Rhys Evans, Nicholas R. Waterfield
pmc-11495950.description: The Photorhabdus virulence cassette (PVC) is an extracellular contractile injection system. In the producing bacterium, N-terminal signal peptides enable effector ‘payloads’ to be loaded into the PVC’s hollow tube—facilitated by the ‘ATPases associated with diverse cellular activities’ (AAA) ATPase, Pvc15—ready for injection of the toxin or virulence factor into eukaryotic cytosols.

pmc-11680374.title: Frequency of Bovine Respiratory Disease Complex Bacterial and Viral Agents Using Multiplex Real-Time qPCR in Quebec, Canada, from 2019 to 2023
pmc-11680374.creator: Sébastien Buczinski, André Broes, Christian Savard, Karl Pedersen
pmc-11680374.description: Simple SummaryThe bovine respiratory disease complex (BRD) is caused by various bacteria and viruses. The objective of this study was to report the proportion of detection for 10 different bovine respiratory infectious agents (6 viruses and 4 bacteria) using two real-time qPCR assays in Quebec, Eastern Canada, during a 5-year period.

pmc-12522611.title: Evaluating performance of the Bioline™ HCV point-of-care test in Ghana
pmc-12522611.creator: Evans Duah, Evans Mantiri Mathebula, Kuhlula Maluleke, Daniel Edem Azumah, Richard Kobina Dadzie Ephraim, Tivani Mashamba-Thompson
pmc-12522611.description: BackgroundHepatitis C Virus (HCV) causes liver diseases including chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), HCV diagnostic resources are limited. Moreover, most evaluations of point-of-care (POC) invitro diagnostics (IVDs) are conducted outside the region using non-African populations, which may not reflect their performance in local settings where they are mostly used.

pmc-13115252.title: Impact of a Multimodal Prehabilitation Program on Perioperative Outcomes in Hepatopancreatobiliary Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13115252.creator: Pipit Burasakarn, Nattaporn Maneepairoj, Vachiraluck Chalokool, Anuparp Thienhiran, Sermsak Hongjinda, Pusit Fuengfoo
pmc-13115252.description: Simple SummaryMajor surgeries involving the liver and pancreas are physically demanding and often lead to long hospital stays. This study investigated whether a four-week “prehabilitation” program—consisting of supervised nutrition, exercise, and mental health support—could better prepare patients for these operations. We found that patients who participated in the program had better nutritional health on the day of surgery.

pmc-13223973.title: Deciphering the single-cell molecular landscape of ampullary cancer: A rare gastrointestinal malignancy
pmc-13223973.creator: Karina Cancino-Maldonado, Ramiro Fernández, Clémentine Decamps, Jenny Bonifacio-Mundaca, Eloy Ruiz, Sandro Casavilca-Zambrano, Pascal Pineau, Frédéric Lopez, Stéphane Bertani, Juan Pablo Cerapio
pmc-13223973.description: SummaryAmpullary carcinoma (AC) is a rare epithelial cancer, representing around 0.2% of all gastrointestinal malignancies worldwide, with an estimated incidence of 0.73 per 100,000 people. The rarity of AC, combined with the intricate anatomy of its site of origin, often complicates histopathological diagnosis. Recent advances in molecular research, however, have begun to illuminate its underlying biological complexity.

pmc-13314420.title: Hemoglobin predicts mortality risk in geriatric patients with dysphagia: a Japanese retrospective cohort study
pmc-13314420.creator: Ping Yuan, Li Zhuo, Jingyi Xue, Xinglin Gao

pmc-13416926.title: Spectral–Structural Collaborative Learning for Fine-Grained Hyperspectral Mineral Classification
pmc-13416926.creator: Yichun Qiu, Yanshuang Zhang, Shixian Cao, Wenyuan Wu, Shanjuan Xie
pmc-13416926.description: Fine-grained hyperspectral mineral classification remains challenging due to spectral homogeneity among minerals with different morphologies, severe spectral mixing from intergrowth, and high dimensionality. Existing methods rely on spectral separability assumptions, which become insufficient when spectral differences are subtle and spatial–structural ambiguity is high. To address these limitations, we propose S3AM-ECA-3DCNN, a spectral–structural collaborative feature learning framework.

pmc-13673129.title: Writing by proxy: Authentic authorship in the era of AI‐powered communication of scientific knowledge
pmc-13673129.creator: Brahim Chaqour
pmc-13673129.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping biomedical research as both a key analytical tool and an efficient copyeditor. Large language models and related algorithms can help investigators sift through the ever‐expanding bodies of scientific literature, connect fragmented biological and clinical datasets, and uncover/recognize meaningful patterns buried within complex multidimensional data.
